subject.title: [Feature]: models.providers.*.enabled flag to disable providers without removing config

question: Should OpenClaw add `models.providers.<provider>.enabled?: boolean` as a persistent provider-routing contract that disables use while preserving the provider config block?
rationale: The request is source-reproducible and useful, but repository policy treats new provider/config/default surfaces as compatibility-sensitive product decisions.

options.title: Approve bounded contract
options.body: Implement default-enabled provider disabling across schema, planning, catalog, fallback, status/probe paths, docs, and focused tests.

options.title: Decline the config knob
options.body: Keep provider removal/editing as the supported workaround and avoid expanding persistent provider config surface.

options.title: Defer for provider design
options.body: Leave the issue open until provider disable, auth ordering, status, and fallback semantics are designed together.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded contract
recommendation.body: Implement default-enabled provider disabling across schema, planning, catalog, fallback, status/probe paths, docs, and focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history across the affected model config/status surfaces and already reviewed this issue in detail.
